One installer, one application image, four deployment modes.

| You want to… | Mode | Command |

| a public server with Traefik + ACME | `server` | `sudo ./install.sh --mode server --domain x.example.com --acme-email ops@example.com --provider deepseek --key sk-...` |

## What runs

One container:

* FastAPI API + background worker (supervisord);
* nginx serving the compiled SPA and proxying `/api` to the API process
  (`--mode dev` replaces nginx with the Vite dev server);
* embedded LanceDB for knowledge/RAG.

There is **no Milvus, LocalAI, LiteLLM, vLLM, Coolify, Prometheus, Caddy or
default workspace**. Coworking/browser/desktop sessions are optional and use the
Docker socket; the installer enables them with `--coworking`.

Every released image is **complete**: it includes the document/OCR tools
(pandoc, TeX Live, tesseract), ffmpeg, Playwright/Chromium and the local
embeddings stack. There is no slim variant.

## Interactive setup

Run the installer with no arguments on a terminal and it asks for every
deployment setting, showing the current value as the default:

```bash
sudo ./install.sh
```

It always asks for the **Traefik setup** (`none` / `master` / `slave`) in
addition to the mode (`local` / `server` / `slave` / `dind` / `dev`), domain, DIND inner
mode, master proxy network/resolver/entrypoint, instance, installation root,
projects folder, port, AI provider and key, coworking and Sysbox. Press Enter to
accept a default. This is what allows combinations such as **dind + local +
slave**: local access on `127.0.0.1:19981` plus a slave Traefik for a master.
`--interactive` forces the wizard even when other flags are present;
`--non-interactive` (or `--yes`) always disables it.

`--mode dev` runs the checkout you are editing instead of a release copy:

```bash
cd ~/codx-junior
./install.sh --mode dev --provider deepseek --key-file ~/.config/codx-junior/deepseek.key
```

* the whole checkout is bind-mounted at `/home/codx-junior/codx-junior`;
* Python changes reload the API (`uvicorn --reload`);
* the SPA is served by the Vite dev server with HMR, not nginx;
* `/api` and Socket.IO are proxied to the API;
* `http://localhost:19981` is ready without rebuilding the image.

The first run builds `codxjuniorai/codx-junior:dev` from the published complete
image plus the client dependencies. Source edits need no rebuild. After changing
`api/pyproject.toml` or `client/package.json`, rerun with `--build`.

Dev is host-only (not available as a DIND inner mode). It still supports
`--traefik slave` if you want localhost and a master URL at the same time.
API reload restarts `uvicorn` on edits, which can interrupt an in-flight agent
turn; that is expected in dev.

## Knowledge / RAG

LanceDB is embedded in the API process. There is no external service:

| `CODX_JUNIOR_KNOWLEDGE_BACKEND` | What runs |
|---|---|
| `lancedb` (default) | embedded, no service |

Dense search needs an embeddings model. `deepseek`, `openrouter` and `groq` do
not provide one, so search runs lexical only on those providers. A missing or
broken embeddings stack degrades to lexical search; it never prevents boot.

## Development

```bash
./dev-install.sh --provider deepseek --key sk-xxxxxxxx
# -> http://localhost:19981
```

Builds the current checkout, mounts it into the same single-container stack and
supports `--reload`, `--build`, `--logs`, `--down` and `--purge`.

## DIND

The wrapper runs its own dockerd and the same runtime compose. Data on the host
lives under `<home>/data` plus `<instance>-dind` (nested image layers). Only one
instance per host can use `--traefik master`; the rest use `--traefik slave`.

`--dind-mode local --traefik slave` is the hybrid: the app is published on
`127.0.0.1:<port>` for local access and the same stack joins the master network
through a slave Traefik.

## Operations

```bash
/opt/codx-junior/bin/codx-junior-compose ps
/opt/codx-junior/bin/codx-junior-compose logs -f
/opt/codx-junior/bin/codx-junior-compose down

sudo ./install.sh --upgrade
sudo ./install.sh status|logs|down|restart|doctor|config|url|env|version
```

On systemd hosts the installer registers `codx-junior.service` (or
`codx-junior-<instance>.service`), and installs a `codx-junior` CLI.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| HTTPS never becomes ready | DNS A record must point at the host; port 80 must be reachable. Check `docker logs -f <instance>-traefik`. |
| port 80/443 already in use | stop the other proxy, or use `--mode slave` |
| UI opens, API disconnected | `bin/codx-junior-compose logs`; check the `api`/`api-background` programs |
| knowledge search is lexical only | configure an embeddings model |
| coworking sessions fail | reinstall with `--coworking --allow-privileged`; VMs also need `/dev/kvm` |
| pull access denied | publish the image to `codxjuniorai/codx-junior`, or use `--build` |
```

```md README.md
# codx-junior installer

One installer, one application image, four deployment modes.

| You want to… | Mode | Command |
|---|---|---|
| try it on a laptop / CI | `local` | `./install.sh --mode local --provider deepseek --key sk-...` |
| a public server with Traefik + ACME | `server` | `sudo ./install.sh --mode server --domain x.example.com --acme-email ops@example.com --provider deepseek --key sk-...` |
| sit behind an existing master proxy | `slave` | `sudo ./install.sh --mode slave --domain x.example.com --proxy-network traefik --provider deepseek --key sk-...` |
| one isolated nested instance per container | `dind` | `sudo ./install.sh --mode dind --dind-mode server --domain x.example.com --acme-email ops@example.com --provider deepseek --key sk-...` |
| DIND with local access **and** a slave proxy | `dind` + `local` + `slave` | `sudo ./install.sh --mode dind --dind-mode local --traefik slave --domain x.example.com --proxy-network traefik --provider deepseek --key sk-...` |
| hack on codx-junior itself, live | `dev` | `./install.sh --mode dev --provider deepseek --key sk-...` |

Design, module audit and known issues:
[`docs/installer-refactor.md`](../docs/installer-refactor.md).

## What runs

One container:

* FastAPI API + background worker (supervisord);
* nginx serving the compiled SPA and proxying `/api` to the API process
  (`--mode dev` replaces nginx with the Vite dev server);
* embedded LanceDB for knowledge/RAG.

There is **no Milvus, LocalAI, LiteLLM, vLLM, Coolify, Prometheus, Caddy or
default workspace**. Coworking/browser/desktop sessions are optional and use the
Docker socket; the installer enables them with `--coworking`.

Every released image is **complete**: it includes the document/OCR tools
(pandoc, TeX Live, tesseract), ffmpeg, Playwright/Chromium and the local
embeddings stack. There is no slim variant.

## Interactive setup

Run the installer with no arguments on a terminal and it asks for every
deployment setting, showing the current value as the default:

```bash
sudo ./install.sh
```

It always asks for the **Traefik setup** (`none` / `master` / `slave`) in
addition to the mode (`local` / `server` / `slave` / `dind` / `dev`), domain, DIND inner
mode, master proxy network/resolver/entrypoint, instance, installation root,
projects folder, port, AI provider and key, coworking and Sysbox. Press Enter to
accept a default. This is what allows combinations such as **dind + local +
slave**: local access on `127.0.0.1:19981` plus a slave Traefik for a master.
`--interactive` forces the wizard even when other flags are present;
`--non-interactive` (or `--yes`) always disables it.

## Development mode

`--mode dev` runs the checkout you are editing instead of a release copy:

```bash
cd ~/codx-junior
./install.sh --mode dev --provider deepseek --key-file ~/.config/codx-junior/deepseek.key
```

* the whole checkout is bind-mounted at `/home/codx-junior/codx-junior`;
* Python changes reload the API (`uvicorn --reload`);
* the SPA is served by the Vite dev server with HMR, not nginx;
* `/api` and Socket.IO are proxied to the API;
* `http://localhost:19981` is ready without rebuilding the image.

The first run builds `codxjuniorai/codx-junior:dev` from the published complete
image plus the client dependencies. Source edits need no rebuild. After changing
`api/pyproject.toml` or `client/package.json`, rerun with `--build`.

Dev is host-only (not available as a DIND inner mode). It still supports
`--traefik slave` if you want localhost and a master URL at the same time.
API reload restarts `uvicorn` on edits, which can interrupt an in-flight agent
turn; that is expected in dev.

## One line: install or update

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/codx-junior/codx-junior/main/install.sh \
  | sudo bash -s -- --provider deepseek --key sk-xxxxxxxx
```

Without `--domain` this serves plain HTTP on the published port. Add
`--domain x.example.com --acme-email ops@example.com` for Traefik + ACME.
Re-running is the upgrade path; projects and settings are kept.

| Situation | Command |
|---|---|
| server with TLS | add `--domain x.example.com --acme-email ops@example.com` |
| localhost / CI | add `--mode local` |
| live codx-junior development | add `--mode dev` |
| behind a master proxy | `--mode slave --domain x.example.com --proxy-network traefik` |
| several instances on one host | `--mode dind --dind-mode server\|slave --instance <name>` |
| branch or tag | add `--branch my-feature` |
| see before acting | add `--dry-run` |
| no internet | `git clone`, then `./install.sh --provider … --key …` |

Only `--provider` and `--key` are required. Providers: `openai`, `deepseek`,
`gemini`, `openrouter`, `mistral`, `groq`, `custom`. Local model servers are not
installed by codx-junior: run Ollama or any other OpenAI-compatible server in a
coworking desktop, then configure it as a `custom` provider.

## Requirements

| | |
|---|---|
| Docker | 20.10+ with the `compose` v2 plugin |
| RAM | 4 GB free; more for coworking desktops or local models |
| Disk | ~8–12 GB for the complete image |
| AI provider | one API key for an OpenAI-compatible provider |

## Image

Images are published under **`codxjuniorai/codx-junior`**:

| Tag | Content |
|---|---|
| `latest` | complete application image (main) |
| `vX.Y.Z` | pinned release |
| `dind` | Docker-in-Docker wrapper (contains the installer and runtime files) |

Publish with the repository script:

```bash
DOCKERHUB_TOKEN=... IMAGE_TAGS="latest" \
  DOCKERFILE=codx-junior-installer/demo/Dockerfile CONTEXT=. \
  ./scripts/dockerhub_publish.sh
```

Or build locally with `./install.sh --build`.

## Knowledge / RAG

LanceDB is embedded in the API process. There is no external service:

| `CODX_JUNIOR_KNOWLEDGE_BACKEND` | What runs |
|---|---|
| `lancedb` (default) | embedded, no service |
| `none` | knowledge disabled |

Dense search needs an embeddings model. `deepseek`, `openrouter` and `groq` do
not provide one, so search runs lexical only on those providers. A missing or
broken embeddings stack degrades to lexical search; it never prevents boot.

wait_for_health() {
  local url=$1 deadline=$(( SECONDS + ${CODX_JUNIOR_WAIT_SECONDS:-180} ))
  command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1 || { warn "curl not found; skipping the health wait"; return 0; }

    if curl -fsS -o /dev/null --max-time 3 "$url"; then printf '\n'; return 0; fi
    printf '.'; sleep 3
  done
  printf '\n'; warn "the stack did not answer on $url within ...; check '$0 --logs'"
  return 1
}

resolve_image() {
  local ref=${1:-} tag
  if [ -z "$ref" ]; then
    printf '%s:%s\n' "$IMAGE_REPO" "$DEFAULT_TAG"
    return 0
  fi
  case $ref in
    *:*) usage_error "--ref takes a tag, not an image reference ($ref)" ;;
  esac
  if [[ $ref =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    tag="v$ref"
  elif [[ $ref =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    tag="$ref"
  elif [[ $ref =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$ ]]; then
    tag="$ref"
  else
    warn "'$ref' is not a valid image tag; using the default tag '$DEFAULT_TAG'"
    tag="$DEFAULT_TAG"
  fi
  printf '%s:%s\n' "$IMAGE_REPO" "$tag"
}

   149| # -> http://localhost:19981
   150| ```
   151| 
   152| Builds the current checkout, mounts it into the same single-container stack and
   153| supports `--reload`, `--build`, `--logs`, `--down` and `--purge`.
   154| 
   155| ## DIND
   156| 
   157| The wrapper runs its own dockerd and the same runtime compose. Data on the host
   158| lives under `<home>/data` plus `<instance>-dind` (nested image layers). Only one
   159| instance per host can use `--traefik master`; the rest use `--traefik slave`.
   160| 
   161| `--dind-mode local --traefik slave` is the hybrid: the app is published on
   162| `127.0.0.1:<port>` for local access and the same stack joins the master network
   163| through a slave Traefik.
   164| 
   165| ## Operations
   166| 
   167| ```bash
   168| /opt/codx-junior/bin/codx-junior-compose ps
   169| /opt/codx-junior/bin/codx-junior-compose logs -f
   170| /opt/codx-junior/bin/codx-junior-compose down
   171| 
   172| sudo ./install.sh --upgrade
   173| sudo ./install.sh status|logs|down|restart|doctor|config|url|env|version
   174| ```
   175| 
   176| On systemd hosts the installer registers `codx-junior.service` (or
   177| `codx-junior-<instance>.service`), and installs a `codx-junior` CLI.
   178| 
   179| ### Whole-repo security scans
   180| 
   181| Whole-repo scans: run them with `docker exec` into `codx-junior-api`; the repo
   182| root is mounted at `/home/codx-junior-projects/codx-junior/codx-junior-platform`.
   183| Fallback container: none verified — the api container is the only place that
   184| root is mounted.
   185| 
   186| ```bash
   187| docker exec codx-junior-api bash -lc 'cd /home/codx-junior-projects/codx-junior/codx-junior-platform && git ls-files | grep -Ei "(^|/)\.env|\.pem$|\.key$|acme|secret"'
   188| ```
   189| 
   190| `git` walks up to the repository root, so the same command also works from
   191| the `codx-junior-installer/` checkout. If `codx-junior-api` is down, start it
   192| with `/opt/codx-junior/bin/codx-junior-compose up -d api` and repeat the scan;

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# demo/up.sh -- one-command bring-up of the codx-junior demo stack.
#
# Uses the single-container stack in demo/docker-compose.yaml: the web UI is
# published on port 19981 (CODX_JUNIOR_WEB_PORT) and the image is the published
# application image, so nothing is compiled on the demo host.
#
# Settings come from demo/.env -- ONE provider and ONE API key, exactly as
# demo/.env.example describes. This script never reads or writes those values:
# it only checks that .env exists.
#
#   ./up.sh                     start the stack and wait until it answers
#   ./up.sh --ref v1.2.3        pin a published image tag
#   ./up.sh --list-providers    show the provider values .env accepts
#   ./up.sh --url               print the URL of a running stack
#   ./up.sh --logs              follow the stack logs
#   ./up.sh --down              stop the stack
#
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd -P)
COMPOSE_FILE="${SCRIPT_DIR}/docker-compose.yaml"
ENV_FILE="${SCRIPT_DIR}/.env"
ENV_EXAMPLE="${SCRIPT_DIR}/.env.example"

IMAGE_REPO="${CODX_JUNIOR_IMAGE_REPO:-codxjuniorai/codx-junior}"
DEFAULT_TAG="${CODX_JUNIOR_TAG:-latest}"
WEB_PORT=19981

ACTION="up"
BUILD=0
WAIT=1
REF=""

die()  { printf 'up.sh: error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
warn() { printf 'up.sh: warning: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
info() { printf 'up.sh: %s\n' "$*"; }
usage_error() {
  printf 'up.sh: error: %s\n' "$*" >&2
  printf "Try '%s --help'.\n" "${0##*/}" >&2
  exit 2
}

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
${0##*/} -- bring the codx-junior demo stack up from a clean checkout

Usage: ${0##*/} [options]

  --ref <tag>         Pin the published image tag. "vX.Y.Z" or "X.Y.Z" both
                      select ${IMAGE_REPO}:vX.Y.Z. Default: ${DEFAULT_TAG}.
  --list-providers    Show the AI provider values demo/.env accepts, then exit.
  --build             Build the image from this checkout instead of pulling it.
  --url               Print the URL of the running stack, then exit.
  --logs              Follow the stack logs, then exit.
  --down              Stop the stack, then exit.
  --no-wait           Do not wait for the stack to answer on /api/health.
  -h, --help          Show this help, then exit.

First run: cp demo/.env.example demo/.env, fill in ONE provider and ONE API key,
then run this script again. The web UI is published on port ${WEB_PORT}.
EOF
}

usage_providers() {
  cat <<'EOF'
AI providers accepted by demo/.env (CODX_JUNIOR_AI_PROVIDER):

  openai       OpenAI-hosted models
  deepseek     DeepSeek chat models
  gemini       Google Gemini models
  openrouter   OpenRouter routing over many upstream models
  mistral      Mistral hosted models
  groq         Groq hosted fast inference
  custom       Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Requires CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL
               too; it must end in /v1
  none         No AI: the UI still starts and AI features stay disabled

Model ids are chosen per provider by codx-junior on first start; override one
with CODX_JUNIOR_AI_MODEL in demo/.env. A local Ollama or any other
OpenAI-compatible server is used as the `custom` provider.

Only the provider and one API key are required -- see demo/.env.example.
EOF
}

# Turns --ref into a full image reference. "1.2.3" and "v1.2.3" both mean the
# published pinned release; an unusable value falls back to the default tag
# instead of failing the demo.
resolve_image() {
  local ref=${1:-} tag
  if [ -z "$ref" ]; then
    printf '%s:%s\n' "$IMAGE_REPO" "$DEFAULT_TAG"
    return 0
  fi
  case $ref in
    */*) usage_error "--ref takes a tag, not an image reference ('$ref')" ;;
  esac
  if [[ $ref =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    tag="v$ref"
  elif [[ $ref =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    tag="$ref"
  elif [[ $ref =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$ ]]; then
    tag="$ref"
  else
    warn "'$ref' is not a usable image tag; using '$DEFAULT_TAG'"
    tag="$DEFAULT_TAG"
  fi
  printf '%s:%s\n' "$IMAGE_REPO" "$tag"
}

compose() { docker compose -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" "$@"; }

host_port() {
  local port
  port=$(compose port codx-junior "$WEB_PORT" 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1s/.*://p') || port=""
  [ -n "$port" ] || port="${CODX_JUNIOR_WEB_PORT:-$WEB_PORT}"
  printf '%s\n' "$port"
}

wait_for_health() {
  local url=$1 timeout=${CODX_JUNIOR_WAIT_SECONDS:-180} waited=0
  if ! command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    warn "curl not found, not waiting for the stack to answer"
    return 0
  fi
  printf 'up.sh: waiting for %s ' "$url"
  while [ "$waited" -lt "$timeout" ]; do
    if curl -fsS --max-time 3 -o /dev/null "$url"; then
      printf 'ready\n'
      return 0
    fi
    printf '.'
    sleep 3
    waited=$((waited + 3))
  done
  printf 'not ready\n'
  warn "the stack did not answer within ${timeout}s; run '${0##*/} --logs'"
  return 1
}

require_docker() {
  command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || die "docker is required for this action ('${0##*/} --list-providers' works without it)"
  docker compose version >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || die "the docker compose v2 plugin is required"
}

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case $1 in
    -h|--help)         usage; exit 0 ;;
    --list-providers)  usage_providers; exit 0 ;;
    --ref)             [ $# -ge 2 ] || usage_error "--ref needs a tag"
                       REF="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --ref=*)           REF="${1#*=}"; shift ;;
    --build)           BUILD=1; shift ;;
    --no-wait)         WAIT=0; shift ;;
    -r)                [ $# -ge 2 ] || usage_error "-r needs a tag"
                       REF="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --url)             ACTION="url"; shift ;;
    --logs)            ACTION="logs"; shift ;;
    --down)            ACTION="down"; shift ;;
    -*)                usage_error "unknown option: $1" ;;
    *)                 usage_error "unexpected argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

[ -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" ] || die "cannot find $COMPOSE_FILE"
require_docker

case $ACTION in
  down)
    info "stopping the demo stack"
    compose down
    exit 0
    ;;
  logs)
    compose logs -f --tail=100
    exit 0
    ;;
  url)
    printf 'http://localhost:%s\n' "$(host_port)"
    exit 0
    ;;
esac

IMAGE_REF=$(resolve_image "$REF")
export CODX_JUNIOR_IMAGE="$IMAGE_REF"
info "image: $IMAGE_REF"

if [ ! -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
  [ -f "$ENV_EXAMPLE" ] || die "both $ENV_FILE and $ENV_EXAMPLE are missing"
  cp "$ENV_EXAMPLE" "$ENV_FILE"
  warn "created $ENV_FILE from .env.example"
  cat >&2 <<EOF
up.sh: fill in CODX_JUNIOR_AI_PROVIDER and CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY in
$ENV_FILE, then run this script again. '${0##*/} --list-providers' prints the
accepted provider values.
EOF
  exit 2
fi

if [ "$BUILD" = "1" ]; then
  info "building $IMAGE_REF from this checkout"
  compose up -d --build
else
  if ! compose pull --ignore-pull-failures codx-junior >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    warn "could not pull $IMAGE_REF; continuing with a local image if present"
  fi
  compose up -d --no-build
fi

url="http://localhost:$(host_port)"
if [ "$WAIT" = "1" ]; then
  wait_for_health "http://127.0.0.1:$(host_port)/api/health" || true
fi

info "web UI: $url"
printf '%s\n' "$url"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# demo/tests/test_up.sh -- executable checks for demo/up.sh
#
# Runs on a host WITHOUT Docker: a shim `docker` on PATH records every call, and
# the script under test is exercised through a temporary "demo" directory built
# from symlinks, so the repository is never touched.
#
#   bash demo/tests/test_up.sh
#
# Output is TAP-like ("ok N - label", "not ok N - label"); the exit code is 0
# only when every check passes.
#
set -uo pipefail

ROOT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd -P)
UP="$ROOT_DIR/demo/up.sh"

WORK=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

SHIM="$WORK/bin"
mkdir -p "$SHIM"
DOCKER_LOG="$WORK/docker.log"
: > "$DOCKER_LOG"

cat > "$SHIM/docker" <<'SHIM_EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
printf '%s\n' "$*" >> "${DOCKER_SHIM_LOG}"
if [ "${1:-}" = "compose" ] && [ "${2:-}" = "port" ]; then
  printf '0.0.0.0:19981\n'
fi
exit 0
SHIM_EOF
chmod +x "$SHIM/docker"

n=0
bad=0
ok()          { n=$((n + 1)); printf 'ok %d - %s\n' "$n" "$1"; }
not_ok()      { n=$((n + 1)); bad=$((bad + 1)); printf 'not ok %d - %s\n' "$n" "$1"; }
check_exit()  { if [ "$2" = "$3" ]; then ok "$1"; else not_ok "$1 (expected exit $3, got $2)"; fi; }
check_has()   { if printf '%s' "$2" | grep -qF -- "$3"; then ok "$1"; else not_ok "$1 (missing: $3)"; fi; }
check_lacks() { if printf '%s' "$2" | grep -qF -- "$3"; then not_ok "$1 (unexpected: $3)"; else ok "$1"; fi; }

# A throwaway "demo" directory: up.sh resolves its own directory, so symlinking
# it here is enough to redirect COMPOSE_FILE / ENV_FILE.
demo_dir() {
  local d="$WORK/demo-$1"
  mkdir -p "$d"
  ln -s "$UP" "$d/up.sh"
  ln -s "$ROOT_DIR/demo/docker-compose.yaml" "$d/docker-compose.yaml"
  ln -s "$ROOT_DIR/demo/.env.example" "$d/.env.example"
  printf '%s\n' "$d"
}

run() { PATH="$SHIM:$PATH" DOCKER_SHIM_LOG="$DOCKER_LOG" bash "$@" 2>&1; }

# 1 -- the script parses
run -n "$UP"
check_exit "bash -n accepts demo/up.sh" "$?" "0"

# 2 -- help documents both flags the README advertises
out=$(run "$UP" --help)
check_exit "--help exits 0" "$?" "0"
check_has "--help documents --list-providers" "$out" "--list-providers"
check_has "--help documents --ref" "$out" "--ref"

# 3 -- providers can be listed with no .env and no Docker running
d=$(demo_dir providers)
: > "$DOCKER_LOG"
out=$(run "$d/up.sh" --list-providers)
check_exit "--list-providers exits 0 without .env" "$?" "0"
check_has "--list-providers lists deepseek" "$out" "deepseek"
check_has "--list-providers lists openrouter" "$out" "openrouter"
check_has "--list-providers lists custom" "$out" "custom"
check_lacks "--list-providers never calls docker" "$(cat "$DOCKER_LOG")" "compose"

# 4 -- an unknown option fails with the usage exit code
d=$(demo_dir badopt)
out=$(run "$d/up.sh" --bogus)
check_exit "an unknown option exits 2" "$?" "2"

# 5 -- an X.Y.Z ref selects the published pinned tag
d=$(demo_dir pin)

#

#   ./up.sh --url               print the URL of a running stack

#   ./up.sh --down              stop the stack

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd -P)
COMPOSE_FILE="${SCRIPT_DIR}/docker-compose.yaml"
ENV_FILE="${SCRIPT_DIR}/.env"
ENV_EXAMPLE="${SCRIPT_DIR}/.env.example"

IMAGE_REPO="${CODX_JUNIOR_IMAGE_REPO:-codxjuniorai/codx-junior}"
DEFAULT_TAG="${CODX_JUNIOR_TAG:-latest}"
WEB_PORT=19981

ACTION="up"
BUILD=0
WAIT=1
REF=""

die()  { printf 'up.sh: error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
warn() { printf 'up.sh: warning: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
info() { printf 'up.sh: %s\n' "$*"; }
usage_error() {
  printf 'up.sh: error: %s\n' "$*" >&2
  printf "Try '%s --help'.\n" "${0##*/}" >&2
  exit 2
}

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
${0##*/} -- bring the codx-junior demo stack up from a clean checkout

Usage: ${0##*/} [options]

  --ref <tag>         Pin the published image tag. "vX.Y.Z" or "X.Y.Z" both
                      select ${IMAGE_REPO}:vX.Y.Z. Default: ${DEFAULT_TAG}.
  --list-providers    Show the AI provider values demo/.env accepts, then exit.
  --build             Build the image from this checkout instead of pulling it.
  --url               Print the URL of the running stack, then exit.
  --logs              Follow the stack logs, then exit.
  --down              Stop the stack, then exit.
  --no-wait           Do not wait for the stack to answer on /api/health.
  -h, --help          Show this help, then exit.

demo/.env is created from demo/.env.example on the first run and holds ONE
provider and ONE API key. The web UI is published on port ${WEB_PORT}.
EOF
}

usage_providers() {
  cat <<'EOF'
AI providers accepted by demo/.env (CODX_JUNIOR_AI_PROVIDER):

  openai       OpenAI-hosted models
  deepseek     DeepSeek chat models
  gemini       Google Gemini models
  openrouter   OpenRouter routing over many upstream models
  mistral      Mistral hosted models
  groq         Groq hosted fast inference
  custom       Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Requires CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL
               too; it must end in /v1
  none         No AI: the UI still starts and AI features stay disabled

Model ids are chosen per provider by codx-junior on first start; override one
with CODX_JUNIOR_AI_MODEL in demo/.env. A local Ollama or any other
OpenAI-compatible server is used as the `custom` provider.

Only the provider and one API key are required -- see demo/.env.example.
EOF
}

# Turns --ref into a full image reference. "1.2.3" and "v1.2.3" both mean the
# published pinned release; an unusable value falls back to the default tag
# instead of failing the demo.
resolve_image() {
  local ref=${1:-} tag
  if [ -z "$ref" ]; then
    printf '%s:%s\n' "$IMAGE_REPO" "$DEFAULT_TAG"
    return 0

  case $ref in
    */*) usage_error "--ref takes a tag, not an image reference ('$ref')" ;;

  if [[ $ref =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    tag="v$ref"
  elif [[ $ref =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    tag="$ref"
  elif [[ $ref =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$ ]]; then
    tag="$ref"

    tag="$DEFAULT_TAG"

    --build)           BUILD=1; shift ;;
    --no-wait)         WAIT=0; shift ;;
    -r)                [ $# -ge 2 ] || usage_error "-r needs a tag"

    --url)             ACTION="url"; shift ;;
    --logs)            ACTION="logs"; shift ;;
    --down)            ACTION="down"; shift ;;
    -*)                usage_error "unknown option: $1" ;;
    *)                 usage_error "unexpected argument: $1" ;;

[ -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" ] || die "cannot find $COMPOSE_FILE"
require_docker

case $ACTION in
  down)
    info "stopping the demo stack"
    compose down
    exit 0
    ;;
  logs)
    compose logs -f --tail=100
    exit 0
    ;;
  url)
    printf 'http://localhost:%s\n' "$(host_port)"
    exit 0
    ;;
esac

IMAGE_REF=$(resolve_image "$REF")
export CODX_JUNIOR_IMAGE="$IMAGE_REF"
info "image: $IMAGE_REF"

if [ ! -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
  [ -f "$ENV_EXAMPLE" ] || die "both $ENV_FILE and $ENV_EXAMPLE are missing"
  cp "$ENV_EXAMPLE" "$ENV_FILE"
  warn "created $ENV_FILE from .env.example"
  cat >&2 <<EOF
up.sh: $ENV_FILE holds CODX_JUNIOR_AI_PROVIDER and CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY.
up.sh: the stack starts once those two values are present in that file.
up.sh: '${0##*/} --list-providers' prints the accepted provider values.
EOF
  exit 2
fi

if [ "$BUILD" = "1" ]; then
  info "building $IMAGE_REF from this checkout"
  compose up -d --build
else
  if ! compose pull --ignore-pull-failures codx-junior >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    warn "could not pull $IMAGE_REF; continuing with a local image if present"
  fi
  compose up -d --no-build
fi

url="http://localhost:$(host_port)"
if [ "$WAIT" = "1" ]; then
  wait_for_health "http://127.0.0.1:$(host_port)/api/health" || true
fi

info "web UI: $url"
printf '%s\n' "$url"
